summary: Standing Sequoia NF lookout on Breckenridge Peak: 1912 tree stand, 1942 L-4 cab on steel tower, NHLR-registered 2001; staffed in fire season per a 2013 page.

facts.design: L-4 cab with catwalk on a 40 ft steel tower per the NHLR; fire-lookouts.org calls the present cab a C-3 style live-in cab

access.note: fire-lookouts.org says the lookout is staffed full time in fire season and generally open to the public; that page was last updated March 1, 2013. No newer confirmation found.

visit.trail_note: Forest Service Road 28S62 off the Caliente-Bodfish Road, about 50 miles east of Bakersfield; one blog lists a drive of about 1 hour 30 minutes from Kernville.

events.note: Original lookout: a small, partly enclosed cab (NHLR) or a crow's nest platform in a tree (fire-lookouts.org) on the summit.
November 1930 Bakersfield Californian report: a 14 x 14 ft lookout on a 24 ft tower. Dates for the wooden tower conflict; see resolved_conflicts.
Melvin Marshall at the lookout; 400 visitors since May 11 per an August 3, 1931 newspaper item.
Ross Shaw stationed at the ranger lookout station on Mount Breckenridge, per a July 30, 1935 newspaper item.
NHLR: wooden tower with an L-4 cab replaced the 1912 tree stand. The blog dates the wooden tower to 1931.
Present cab: L-4 with catwalk on a 40 ft steel tower (NHLR); fire-lookouts.org says built 1942 by the Civilian Conservation Corps, as a C-3 style cab.
Blog only: wooden tower used until 1944, then replaced with a structure built by the CCC. Conflicts with the NHLR and fire-lookouts.org dates; see resolved_conflicts.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on June 10, 2001 (US 378).

Forest Fire Lookout Association 2009 report: the forest fire management officer found lightning protection at Breckenridge not operationally sound; the forest contracted a grounding inspection and repairs for its remaining lookouts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR calls the present cab an L-4 with catwalk on a 40 ft steel tower; fire-lookouts.org calls it a C-3 style live-in cab. Both are reported in the story and neither is chosen.

Dates for the wooden tower and its replacement disagree: 1930 newspaper (lookout house on a 24 ft tower), 1931 blog (wooden tower built next to the tree), 1938 NHLR (wooden tower with L-4 cab), and 1944 blog (replaced by a CCC structure) against 1942 NHLR and fire-lookouts.org for the present cab. Story says the accounts differ.

NHLR gives 7,386 ft (2,251 m), matching the record's 2251.3 m. fire-lookouts.org and the blog give 7,548 ft, and the 1930 newspaper gives about 8,000 ft. The record was kept and the story gives no elevation.

notes_for_editor: Standing lookout; the record's 1942 build date matches the NHLR and fire-lookouts.org for the present cab, so no correction is proposed. Sources disagree on the cab style (L-4 vs C-3), the wooden tower dates (1930/1931/1938) and elevation (7,386 vs 7,548 vs about 8,000 ft). The staffed and open-to-public status comes from a page last updated 2013; NHLR says in active service but gives no date. No 2026 confirmation was found. The weebly page has the 1928-1935 newspaper items. The Living New Deal page returned 403, so it was not read. Story is about 365 words including footnotes.
